fields.ic_name: AMBA AXI / ACE Protocol Specification (ARM IHI 0022E)

clock_and_reset_waveform.ACLK: Single rising-edge clock per ACE interface (master, slave, interconnect, snoop ports all share the same ACLK or are bridged via synchronizers).
clock_and_reset_waveform.ARESETn: Active LOW. Async assert; sync deassert. After ARESETn=HIGH, earliest rising ACLK edge that any VALID (AR/AW/W/CR/CD) may be asserted = next rising edge.

handshake_waveforms_inherited_axi.sequence: Source asserts VALID at T1. Destination asserts READY at T2. Transfer at T3.
Destination asserts READY at T1. Source asserts VALID at T2. Single-cycle transfer at T3.

handshake_waveforms_inherited_axi.case: VALID with READY same cycle (Figure A3-4)
handshake_waveforms_inherited_axi.sequence: Both VALID and READY assert at T1. Transfer at T2.

arrows: ACVALID -> ACREADY (single-headed; can precede or follow)
ACVALID + ACREADY -> CRVALID (double-headed; master must wait both before asserting CRVALID)
ACVALID + ACREADY -> CDVALID (double-headed; master must wait both before asserting CDVALID)
CRVALID + CDVALID (if DataTransfer=1) -> interconnect can wait either or both before completing the snoop
ACVALID must not depend on ACREADY (deadlock prevention)
CRVALID/CDVALID must not depend on CRREADY/CDREADY

sequence: T0: Master M0 drives AR* (ARDOMAIN, ARSNOOP, ARBAR + ARADDR/ARLEN/ARSIZE); asserts ARVALID.
T1: ARREADY HIGH at rising edge — AR handshake complete.
T2+: Interconnect issues snoops on AC channel to other masters (parallel to fetch from final destination).
T3+: Other masters drive ACREADY HIGH; then deliver CRRESP on CR and (if DataTransfer=1) CDDATA on CD.
T5+: Interconnect aggregates snoop results + final data; drives R channel beats with RDATA + RRESP[3:2] PassDirty/IsShared.
T9: Master asserts RREADY per beat; RLAST=1 on the final beat.
T10 (one cycle after RLAST handshake): Master asserts RACK for one ACLK cycle.
Master installs cache line per (RRESP[3:2], chosen ARSNOOP) per Table C5-4.
T0: Master drives AW* including AWDOMAIN/AWSNOOP/AWBAR; asserts AWVALID.
T0: Master may also drive WDATA[0] + WSTRB + WLAST; asserts WVALID.
T1+: AW and W handshakes complete (in any order).
T5+: After AW + W handshakes + WLAST, slave drives BRESP[2:0] + BVALID.
T6: Master asserts BREADY; B handshake completes.
T7 (one cycle after B handshake): Master asserts WACK for one ACLK cycle.
Transaction complete; interconnect can now safely route dependent snoops.

ace_snoop_dependency_diagram.summary: Interconnect drives ACVALID independent of ACREADY. Master may default ACREADY=HIGH or wait. Master must wait for both ACVALID + ACREADY before CRVALID and CDVALID. If DataTransfer=1, master delivers CD beats (CDDATA + CDLAST) gated by CDREADY.

fields.snoop_response_ordering_rule: Each snoop transaction is fully ordered: a response on CR must be in the same order as the addresses on AC. Master may not reorder snoops issued by the interconnect.

max_outstanding_rules_inherited.same_AxID_ordering: All transactions with the same AXI ID must remain in order.
max_outstanding_rules_inherited.different_AxID_ordering: No ordering constraint between different IDs.
max_outstanding_rules_inherited.ACE_snoop_ordering: Snoop responses on CR (and CD when used) follow the order of snoop addresses on AC.

fields.ace_lite_no_snoop_channels: ACE-Lite masters have no AC/CR/CD channels. Their R/B responses still observe RRESP[3:2] / BRESP[2] extension bits but they never participate in snoop traffic.

evidence.quote: Figure A3-1 shows the earliest point after reset that ARVALID, AWVALID, or WVALID can be driven HIGH.
All five transaction channels use the same VALID/READY handshake process.
The standard AXI VALID/READY handshake rules apply. When CRVALID is asserted it must remain asserted until CRREADY is asserted.
If the CDVALID signal is asserted, the data value on CDDATA and the last transfer indication on CDLAST, must not change until CDREADY is asserted.

evidence.spec_section: C3.9 Snoop channel dependencies / Figure C3-1
evidence.quote: The master must wait for both ACVALID and ACREADY to be asserted before asserting CRVALID. The master must wait for both ACVALID and ACREADY to be asserted before asserting CDVALID.
